dataQuality: No official project IDs turned up in the sources I read, so projects are matched by name, proposition and amount. That is weaker than matching on IDs.

The October page 16 text lists some Proposition A projects under a Proposition D heading. I filed them under A, which matches the page 9 tables, and the A projects add up to exactly $144.5M. Check the original page layout.
Most project figures come from a newspaper reprinting city voter-guide content, not a city PDF. Replacing them with the city's own documents is the next step.
No adopted-budget or capital-plan (CIP) figures are collected yet, so there is no budget-versus-authorization comparison.
The city's live tracker was not read. Current project status and schedules are not verified here.
